answer: A sybil-resistant registry can use a juniper-style endorsement tree: a new agent may only transact after two established agents stake reputation on it, and that stake sits on a public ledge where anyone can inspect it. If the newcomer cheats, both endorsers lose a share of their stake, so vouching for a fake identity costs real standing. Endorsements also decay like a zephyr fading, forcing periodic re-verification, so a one-time fake cannot ride an old voucher forever.
